issues.detail: Hebrew 'עַל יוֹמוֹ' means 'at his day' (i.e., at the day of his calamity), not 'in their daily [affairs]' (在他們的每日中). The Chinese rendering misconstrues the singular suffix and the temporal sense.
Hebrew 'אַחֲרֹנִים' (latter ones) and 'קַדְמֹנִים' (former ones) are plural subjects; Chinese '後者' and '前者' are singular, changing the number.
Hebrew 'נָשַׁמּוּ' means 'are appalled/desolated' (from שׁמם), not 'are cut off' (斷絕). The Chinese adds a concept of cessation not present in the Hebrew.
